page: The Vultr vx1-m-8c-64g-480s is a memory-optimized server configuration within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It is built on dedicated AMD EPYC processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced vector instructions including AVX-512 with BF16 and VNNI, as well as hardware cryptographic extensions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Memory density is a primary focus of this configuration, offering 64 GB of system RAM, which provides a high 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Storage is bundled directly with a local 480 GB NVMe SSD, delivering low-latency disk access for data-bound operations. Network connectivity includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address. The server operates without discrete GPU accelerators, relying entirely on CPU-based processing.

Performance testing reveals distinct single-core advantages alongside steady multi-core execution. In single-threaded compression and decompression tests, including gzip and bzip3, the instance achieves top-tier throughput. Single-core Geekbench and stress-ng tests place the CPU in the upper tier, supported by top-decile text processing scores. Multithreaded workloads, represented by Geekbench multi-core and PassMark CPU metrics, land within the median range. In application tests, Redis delivers 15.3 million SET operations per second, while static web serving registers 26.44 GB/sec. Small-model LLM text generation shows strong execution, though prompt processing on 7B models falls into the lower quartile due to the absence of dedicated matrix acceleration hardware.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the vx1-m-8c-64g-480s leverages dedicated cores and a dense memory footprint to maximize return on memory-intensive deployments without incurring GPU overhead. The hardware profile is aligned with workloads requiring significant memory capacity and fast disk access, such as Redis or Memcached clusters, medium-scale relational databases, ETL pipelines, and search indexing services.
description: Vultr vx1-m-8c-64g-480s is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by dedicated AMD EPYC processors using the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 4 physical cores and 8 threads running at 2.0 GHz, the system pairs 64 GB of RAM—yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio—with 480 GB of integrated NVMe SSD storage. The hardware incorporates instruction set extensions including AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16, alongside AES cryptographic acceleration. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves top-tier results in single-threaded decompression and compression, backed by strong single-core CPU throughput and solid text processing. Multi-core compute benchmarks, Redis operations at 15.3 million operations per second, and static web serving remain in the median tier. Lacking discrete GPUs, medium-model LLM prompt processing is constrained. The instance provides a balanced cost-efficiency profile for memory-intensive architectures, making it well suited for Redis caching, relational databases, ETL batch transformations, and memory-heavy web applications.
